evals.prompt: The roadmap says RAG is a later extension after the read-only foundation is reliable. I want Lesson 11 on that — retrieving relevant material before answering, applied to IBM i source and docs. Write it and make sure it shows up in the roadmap and the index.
evals.expected_output: A new docs/lesson-11-*.md that matches the house chapter structure, plus rows added to the roadmap and learning-index tables.
assertions: Creates a new chapter file named docs/lesson-11-<slug>.md
H1 reads '# Lesson 11 — <Title>' using an em dash
Line 3 is the nav line beginning '[Learning index](README.md)'
Carries a bold '**Project milestone:**' or '**Project connection:**' line in the first 12 lines
Ends with a '## Summary' containing a paired **English:** / **Hinglish:** line
Every **Hinglish:** line is Roman script with no Devanagari characters
Includes a paper walkthrough that traces a fictional request in numbered steps
Uses the house fictional identifiers (APPLIB, DEV, or an established tool name from the Phase 1 catalogue)
Adds a row for Lesson 11 to the chapter table in docs/00-roadmap.md
Adds a row for Lesson 11 to the chapter table in docs/README.md
All relative links in the new chapter resolve to real files
Frames RAG as a later extension rather than claiming it is built or available today

evals.prompt: Lesson 6 is too thin on program references. Add a proper section on why recorded DSPPGMREF-style references miss runtime dependencies — service programs bound at runtime, dynamic calls, SQL routines — with a paper walkthrough that shows the gap.
evals.expected_output: An expanded docs/lesson-06-inspection-tools.md with a new section and walkthrough, with the chapter's existing structure preserved.
assertions: Preserves the original H1, nav line, and '**Project milestone:**' line unchanged
Adds substantive new content on runtime dependency gaps covering at least service programs, dynamic calls, and SQL routines
New content includes a walkthrough using fictional IBM i identifiers in the house style
The **English:** and **Hinglish:** lines remain present and equal in number
States explicitly what recorded references do NOT establish, rather than only what they show
Passes check_lessons.py with zero errors
Leaves unrelated sections of Lesson 6 substantially untouched
Keeps the roadmap and learning-index descriptions of Lesson 6 consistent with the revised chapter

evals.prompt: Can you go through docs/ and tell me if the lessons have drifted apart? I've been editing them piecemeal and I think some conventions have slipped.
evals.expected_output: A report naming real, verifiable convention variations across all ten chapters, separating genuine drift from legitimate variation.
assertions: Covers all ten lesson chapters, not a sample
Identifies at least one real, verifiable variation present in the actual files
Reports no fabricated findings — every issue named can be confirmed in the source files
Distinguishes genuine drift from legitimate variation rather than flagging every difference as a defect

Delivers a report without rewriting the lesson files
